summary:
Our project is an interactive educational space game designed for children aged 9–16, aiming to make learning about space fun, engaging, and accessible.

The game features three main missions: Space Rescue, where players rescue stranded astronauts while avoiding asteroids; Mars Base, where they manage oxygen, collect resources, and repair solar stations to help a Martian colony survive; and Solar Map, where they freely explore the solar system and discover fascinating facts about planets and stars.

Our solution addresses the challenge of making space science more engaging and understandable for younger generations by transforming complex scientific concepts into interactive experiences.

It is important because it combines education with entertainment, helping children develop scientific curiosity, problem-solving, critical thinking, coordination, and teamwork while learning about astronomy, physics, space exploration, and the challenges of living beyond Earth.

What We Built (High-Level Summary)

Our project is an interactive educational space game designed for children aged 9–16, aiming to make learning about space fun, engaging, and accessible. The game combines education and entertainment through exciting missions that allow players to explore space, solve problems, and discover scientific facts while enjoying an immersive gaming experience.

How It Addresses the Challenge

Space science can sometimes be difficult for younger generations to understand because many scientific concepts are complex and traditionally taught through textbooks and theoretical explanations. Our project addresses this challenge by transforming complex scientific concepts into interactive and enjoyable gaming experiences. Instead of simply reading about space, children can explore it, complete missions, overcome challenges, and learn through direct interaction.
